summary.prose: The curated catalog file shipped with insrc becomes the one place that describes the Claude CLI, Codex CLI and Ollama families: every selectable model with its aliases, effort levels and input limit, each family's tier defaults and summariser model, and the default local model. The daemon checks it at startup, every daemon thread reads it the way settings are read today, and the settings defaults are taken from it, so no model name is left in code. Clients ask the daemon for it, an unknown Claude or Codex model is used only after the user approves a check of it, and tiers become global-only. Like saved settings today, a change applies at the next daemon restart.

body.frameworkSummary: The curated cloud catalog keeps its file (src/assets/models/cloud-model-catalog.json), its loader (validateModelCatalog, src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:162) and its boot hook (src/daemon/index.ts:381), as the DEF decided, and is extended into the model definitions: exactly one entry for each built-in family, each with its CLI kind (CLI families), its selectable models with aliases, accepted efforts and input limit, its tier defaults and summariser model (CLI families), the Ollama tool-loop default, and the default family. Each Ollama model's input limit is its context window and replaces the global models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx; the output cap ollamaNumPredict stays global. A ModelRegistry built from the file and the per-user approved-model store answers every model question in the daemon; each thread builds and caches it the way it loads and caches settings today (src/config/analyze.ts:234), so the file, an approval or a saved tier applies at the next daemon restart, as saved settings already do. The settings catalog takes the defaults of its tier runner, tier model and local coreModel rows, and the allowed effort values, from the same file, so reconcile, the updater, the settings catalog loader and older plugins keep working unchanged and no model name stays in code. One read-only request, models.definitions, serves the definitions to clients and is the source of providers.listModels; models.resolveRole lets the TUI's review command run the model the daemon would. Unknown Claude and Codex models are checked through their CLI one call at a time and recorded only on the user's approval, and only for a check in which the model ran. A tier set to a model that is neither listed nor approved runs a tier default with a warning (decision A). Tiers become global-only; a repo keeps `tasks` and coreFloor. Settings-write safety is out of scope (ISSUE-8dc75bc5).
body.architectureShape: Definitions (s1): the extended catalog file and its validator (src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:107-162), run by the existing boot hook before the daemon listens (src/daemon/index.ts:381); the ModelRegistry, built in each thread from the file and the approved-model store on first use and cached for the thread's life, like loadAnalyzeConfig (src/config/analyze.ts:234). The main thread validates the file before it starts the worker threads, so a worker reads an already validated file. Daemon consumers (s3): tier resolution (resolveTiers and resolveTier over DEFAULT_TIERS, src/config/analyze.ts:135-137), the summariser fallback (src/analyze/context/shaper-provider.ts:271), the effort list (TIER_EFFORTS, src/config/analyze.ts:115), CliProvider's input budget and CLI kind (src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:181, :202-204), the Ollama context window (src/analyze/context/shaper-provider.ts:267, :303, src/analyze/context/driver.ts:531, :833), the tool-loop model (src/analyze/context/driver.ts:1100) and the runner literals in routing, provider construction, attribution and workflow code all ask the registry. The settings catalog's tier and coreModel rows (src/config/config-catalog.ts:113-118, :142) and the local settings default (src/config/local.ts:53) take their values from the definitions; reconcile (src/config/reconcile.ts:379) keeps filling them as it does today; reconcile also removes per-repo tier overrides and prunes ollamaNumCtx, and readRepoOverride (src/config/analyze.ts:444-463) and its callers (src/daemon/workflow-rpc.ts:35, src/daemon/code-review-rpc.ts:194) go away. config.write (src/daemon/handler-runtime.ts:1278) refuses a tier set to a rejected model and reports restartRequired for a model setting. A model that is listed but not installed in Ollama fails at the call, as today (src/agent/providers/ollama.ts:375). IPC: models.definitions (s2) projects the registry, adds each listed Ollama model's installed state from the existing bounded listing (src/daemon/list-models.ts:113), and providers.listModels (src/daemon/list-models.ts:127) is drawn from it; models.check / models.approve / models.reject (s4) drive the unknown-model flow; models.resolveRole (s3) serves the TUI review (src/cli/services/workflow.ts:248-253); each new method is classified in src/daemon/threads/method-class.ts. Clients (s5-s7): the TUI model-tiers pane, review command and Setup (which drops DEFAULT_LOCAL_MODEL, src/shared/model-recommender.ts:22), the VS Code picker and repo panel, and the JetBrains model-tiers and per-repo settings render models.definitions, use the check and approval requests, show restartRequired, and offer the daemon restart where the client has one (src/cli/services/maintenance.ts:284, vscode-plugin/src/daemon/commands.ts:26). Installer: both copies take the chosen family's tier defaults and the tool-loop default from the file (scripts/insrc-daemon-install.sh:291-297, :324, :351).

sharedContracts.name: ModelDefinitionsFile (the curated catalog file, extended)
sharedContracts.purpose: The shipped, versioned data format of src/assets/models/cloud-model-catalog.json: the only place model facts and default model choices are stated (k4). Validated at daemon start (k7); a change applies at the next restart (s1/ac2). Ollama models must be listed to be selectable.

sharedContracts.name: ModelRegistry and the approved-model store
sharedContracts.purpose: The in-process view every daemon consumer asks, built from the sc1 file plus the per-user approved-model store and cached per thread like settings. Defines the store's entry shape (written by s4). Resolves aliases, accepted efforts, input limits and defaults, and applies decision A.

sharedContracts.name: models.definitions IPC request
sharedContracts.purpose: The one read-only request clients use to learn the definitions (k2): families with CLI kind and rejected ids, models with aliases, efforts and limits and whether they are shipped or user-approved, tier defaults, summariser model, tool-loop default, default family, and each listed Ollama model's installed state. providers.listModels is drawn from the same registry (s2/ac2).

sharedContracts.name: Unknown-model check and approval requests
sharedContracts.purpose: Checks a Claude or Codex model that is not in the definitions through its CLI, one call at a time (k1, k3), returns per-effort evidence, and records the user's decision as an ApprovedProfile (sc2) outside the shipped file and config.json (k4, k5). Approval is accepted only for a check in which the model ran without error. A decision applies at the next daemon restart, which the result says. Ollama has no such flow: only listed Ollama models are selectable.

sharedContracts.name: Settings rules and models.resolveRole
sharedContracts.purpose: What changes in settings: the settings catalog's tier runner, tier model and local coreModel defaults and the allowed effort values come from the definitions; per-repo tier overrides are removed with a warning (k6, s3/ac5); ollamaNumCtx is pruned; config.write refuses a tier set to a rejected model (s4/ac4) and reports restartRequired for model settings. models.resolveRole gives the TUI's review command the tier, model, effort and provider settings the daemon would use for a role and repo.

storyBoundaries.internal: Extending the catalog file, its types (CloudModelCatalogFile, src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:48) and its validator in place; refreshing its contents with today's models, the aliases today's tier defaults use (opus, sonnet, haiku), the Ollama models insrc ships with and their context windows, and today's coreModel as the tool-loop default; the registry and its per-thread cache; reading the approved-model store (a malformed store is logged and treated as empty). The validator refuses a missing or malformed file, an unknown, missing or repeated family, a CLI family without its CLI kind, tier defaults or summariser model, a model without an efforts list, a duplicate id or alias, a default that is not a model of its family, an Ollama model without a token input limit, and a tool-loop default that is not listed, naming the entry (ac3). Tests: one fixture per refusal reason (ac3); a model and alias added to a fixture are served after a restart with no code change (ac2); the file is validated before the worker threads start and before listen (ac1, k7); alias, effort and limit lookups; resolveTier distinguishes rejected-model from unlisted-model and falls back to the tier's family default, or the default family's for an Ollama tier.

The models.definitions handler and its method-class entry, the projection of the registry, each listed Ollama model's installed state from the existing bounded listing, and re-sourcing providers.listModels from the registry (for Ollama, listed models only). Tests: models.definitions returns every field of a fixture file (ac1); providers.listModels and models.definitions agree for every family, and an installed but unlisted Ollama model appears in neither (ac2); with Ollama not answering, installed is absent and the request still succeeds.

Moving every daemon consumer onto the registry: tier resolution, summariser selection, effort forwarding, CliProvider's input budget and CLI kind, OllamaProvider's num_ctx, the tool-loop model (an unlisted coreModel runs the tool-loop default with a warning) and the runner and model literals in routing, provider construction, attribution and workflow code; DEFAULT_TIERS, TIER_EFFORTS, SUMMARISER_CLI_FALLBACK, CODEX_INPUT_BUDGET_CHARS and ollamaNumCtx go. The settings catalog's tier and coreModel defaults and effort values are taken from the definitions; how the settings catalog reaches the file is decided in this Story's LLD and must work in every process that loads the settings catalog today (the daemon, the TUI, the updater, and the VS Code bundle until s6 drops its use). Reconcile removes per-repo tier overrides with a warning and prunes ollamaNumCtx; readRepoOverride and its callers go. config.write refuses a tier set to a rejected model and reports restartRequired. models.resolveRole and its method-class entry. Both installer copies take tier defaults and the tool-loop default from the file. Tests: an unset tier resolves to the file's default, and with a fixture whose defaults differ from today's, reconcile fills the fixture's values (ac1); an unsupported effort is dropped with a warning naming model and effort (ac2); a source scan fails on runner or model literals outside the family implementations and on any read of ollamaNumCtx (ac3); a repo's `tasks` choice applies with the global tier's model (ac4); reconcile removes per-repo tier overrides with a warning naming repo and tier and keeps `tasks` and coreFloor (ac5); an unlisted model falls back with the warning (decision A); a fixture Ollama model's input limit sets num_ctx; config.write refuses a rejected model and reports restartRequired; models.resolveRole matches the daemon's own resolution for a CLI tier and an Ollama tier; the settings catalog loader accepts the catalog and an unset JetBrains tier still shows the default family's values.

The per-family check procedures (Codex: the CLI's model list plus a run; Claude: a run, the input limit from the JSON output, recognised effort names), run one call at a time; telling a reachable CLI that refuses the model apart from an unreachable CLI; refusing approval unless the model ran without error; writing the store atomically and acknowledging a decision only once it is written; the method-class entries. Tests: checks against fake CLIs record each verdict and run one at a time (ac1); results list each claimed level with evidence and nothing is usable before approval (ac2); after approval and a restart only the approved levels are accepted (ac3); a rejected profile or unreachable CLI refuses the model with a reason, and approving a check whose model did not run is refused (ac4); after a restart an approved model appears in models.definitions as user-approved and a rejected one among the rejected ids (ac5); a failed store write returns write-failed and keeps the previous store.

The TUI model-tiers pane and its effort choices from models.definitions; the unknown-model check and approval screen; the repo settings view limited to `tasks` and coreFloor; showing restartRequired and offering maintenance.restart; the review command using models.resolveRole and building its provider from the answer instead of reading config.json; Setup recommending the definitions' tool-loop default instead of DEFAULT_LOCAL_MODEL, and saying it cannot recommend when the daemon is not running. Tests: the pane offers exactly the options of a fake models.definitions answer (ac1); saving an unknown model starts the check and shows its results (ac2); the repo view edits only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3); the review command runs the model a fake models.resolveRole returns for a CLI and an Ollama tier; Setup recommends the fake answer's tool-loop default.

The VS Code model-tier picker driven by models.definitions instead of its runner list and the bundled settings catalog's effort rows; the unknown-model check and approval prompt; the Repo Configuration panel without per-tier fields; showing restartRequired and offering insrc.daemon.restart. Tests: the picker offers exactly a fake answer's options and the bundle keeps no runner or model list (ac1); an unknown model is saved only after approval (ac2); the repo panel shows only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3).

The JetBrains model-tiers section driven by models.definitions instead of ModelTiersModel.PROVIDERS; the unknown-model check and approval dialog; the per-repo settings without per-tier fields; showing restartRequired. Tests: the section offers exactly a fake answer's options and the plugin keeps no runner or model list (ac1); an unknown model is saved only after approval (ac2); the per-repo settings show only `tasks` and coreFloor (ac3).

nonFunctional.performance: The file is parsed once per thread and every model question is an in-memory lookup; models.definitions touches no CLI and makes one bounded Ollama listing call, the same one providers.listModels makes today.
nonFunctional.security: No cloud REST call is added (k1): checks run only through the installed claude and codex CLIs. The approved-model store is a per-user file under the insrc home written only by the daemon; clients reach it only through models.approve and models.reject (k2).
nonFunctional.observability: A bad file stops the daemon with a log naming the entry (s1/ac3); a dropped effort logs model and effort (s3/ac2); a tier fallback logs tier, requested model, reason and the default used (decision A); a tool-loop substitution logs both models; removing a per-repo tier override logs repo and tier (s3/ac5); each CLI call of a check and its verdict is logged.
nonFunctional.durability: Approved and rejected profiles live outside the shipped file and config.json, so they survive restarts and updates; the store is replaced atomically and a decision is acknowledged only once written; a malformed store is logged and treated as empty. When an update ships a model the user had approved, the shipped definition wins. Existing `tasks`, coreFloor, ollamaNumPredict and every tier value already in config.json are kept.

phases.name: Phase A — definitions file and registry
phases.rationale: s1 owns sc1 and sc2, which every other Story consumes; it has no dependencies.
phases.backwardCompat: The catalog file, loader and boot hook stay where they are and keep their fail-fast refusal. The file keeps today's Claude and Codex entries (stale ids refreshed) and adds the aliases today's tier defaults use, so every tier already set to opus, sonnet, haiku or a listed Codex id still resolves; the Ollama tool-loop default is today's coreModel default, so nothing that runs changes.

phases.name: Phase B — daemon serves and runs by the definitions
phases.rationale: Both depend only on s1. s2 adds models.definitions and re-sources providers.listModels; s3 moves every daemon consumer onto the registry, derives the settings defaults from the file, makes tiers global-only and adds models.resolveRole.
phases.backwardCompat: providers.listModels, config.write and config.catalog keep their shapes; config.write adds restartRequired and a rejected-model refusal. Settings rows keep defaults, now taken from the file with today's values, so reconcile, the updater's catalog loader and older plugins behave as before. Tier values already in config.json stay and keep running. Deliberate changes: a repo's per-repo tier override, including the core runner/model override read fresh today, is removed with a warning (k6); a tier set to an unlisted, unapproved model runs a tier default with a warning (decision A); ollamaNumCtx is pruned and each Ollama model's context window comes from the file. Until s6 lands, the VS Code bundle still carries the settings catalog.

phases.name: Phase C — unknown-model check and approval
phases.rationale: s4 depends on s2 (approved and rejected models appear in models.definitions) and lands before the clients that drive it.
phases.backwardCompat: A tier that fell back keeps running its default until the user approves the requested model and the daemon restarts.

phases.name: Phase D — clients render the daemon's definitions
phases.rationale: Each client Story depends on s2, s3 and s4 and on nothing from the others, so they can land in any order.
phases.backwardCompat: An older plugin keeps working against the new daemon because providers.listModels, config.catalog and config.write keep their shapes and keys; it shows its own lists until updated and ignores restartRequired. Until s5 lands, the TUI review resolves its model as today.

rolloutOverview.orderingRationale: Owners before consumers: s1 (sc1, sc2); then s2 (sc3) and s3 (sc5), which need only s1; then s4 (sc4), which needs sc3; then the three clients. This follows the Epic's dependsOn edges.

riskyBits.area: Settings defaults taken from the file (s3)
riskyBits.why: The settings catalog is loaded by the daemon, the TUI, the updater's catalog loader (which requires a default on every row, src/config/config-catalog-loader.ts:41) and, until s6, the VS Code bundle (vscode-plugin/src/models/model-tier-picker.ts:25); a way of reaching the file that works in one of them may fail in another.
riskyBits.mitigation: s3's LLD decides the mechanism against all four; tests load the settings catalog through the updater's loader and check an unset JetBrains tier still shows the default family's values.

riskyBits.why: About 30 files import src/config/analyze.ts and 14 carry runner literals; a missed literal keeps a second source of truth.
riskyBits.mitigation: A source scan test fails on any runner or model literal outside the family implementations and on any read of ollamaNumCtx (s3/ac3).

alternativesConsidered.name: Extend the curated catalog into the one definitions file, read through the existing load paths
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Extend the curated catalog file, loader and boot hook in place to hold every model fact and default for all three families; daemon code reads it through a registry each thread loads and caches as settings are today, the settings catalog takes its tier and local-model defaults from it, and clients read it over IPC.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
The curated catalog keeps its file, loader and boot hook (as the DEF decided) and gains, per family, its CLI kind, its selectable models with aliases, accepted efforts and input limit, its tier defaults and summariser model, the Ollama tool-loop default and the default family; it replaces the global ollamaNumCtx with each Ollama model's own context window. The boot hook validates it before the daemon listens. Each thread loads it, with the approved-model store, through one registry and caches it for its lifetime, exactly as settings are loaded and cached today, so a change applies at the next daemon restart, as settings changes already do. The settings catalog takes the default of the tier runner, tier model and local coreModel rows from the same file, so reconcile, the updater's catalog loader and older plugins keep working unchanged and no model name is written in code.

One read-only IPC request serves the definitions and is the source of providers.listModels; a second resolves a role for the TUI's review command. Unknown Claude and Codex models are checked through their CLI one call at a time and recorded in a per-user store only on the user's approval, and only for a check in which the model ran. A tier set to a model that is neither listed nor approved runs its family's tier default with a warning (decision A). Tiers become global-only; a repo keeps `tasks` and coreFloor.
pros: Every model fact and default is in one data file; adding a model, alias, effort level or limit is a file edit and a restart (s1/ac2).
Reuses today's load-and-cache behaviour and settings defaults mechanism, so reconcile, the updater, the settings catalog loader and older plugins need no new rules.
Clients reach the facts only over IPC (k2), so a new model or effort level needs no plugin release once s5-s7 land.
cons: Wide but mechanical migration: about 30 files import src/config/analyze.ts and 14 carry runner literals.
A change to the file, an approval or a saved tier applies only after a daemon restart, as saved settings do today; clients must say so.
A fresh install keeps the defaults it got at its first start, since reconcile writes them into config.json; a later default change reaches it only through aliases or a user change.

alternativesConsidered.name: Build-time code generation from one data file
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep one shipped data file but compile it into generated TypeScript constants that the daemon and the VS Code extension import, with JetBrains reading the same facts over IPC.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
A build step turns the definitions file into a generated module of typed constants that the daemon and the VS Code extension import; JetBrains receives the same facts over IPC.

Unknown-model approvals are handled at run time by the daemon in a separate store and merged where it resolves a tier.
pros: A model removed from the data file breaks the build where it was used.
cons: Breaks k2 for VS Code: the extension keeps a compiled copy, so a model or effort change still needs a VS Code release.
A data-file edit needs a regenerated module and rebuild of every TypeScript consumer.
A hand-edited installed file is not checked at start (k7).
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates k2 and only partially meets k4 and k7.

alternativesConsidered.name: Definitions seeded into the user's settings
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Ship a defaults file whose contents reconcile copies into each user's config.json, and read model facts from the settings every consumer already loads.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
The shipped defaults describe families, models, efforts and limits; reconcile copies them into config.json on boot and update, and consumers read them from settings.

User-approved models are added to the same settings section.
pros: Reuses the existing settings load and reconcile path.
cons: Violates k4: model facts live in the user's config.json.
A shipped update must be merged into every user's edited copy.
Users can hand-edit a model's efforts, so the daemon could run a capability the model lacks (weakens k5).
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates k4 and weakens k5 and k7.

alternativesConsidered.name: Boot snapshot handed to every worker, with no settings defaults (HLD revisions 9-11)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1, but the main thread reads every model input once into a snapshot carried to each worker in its start data, the settings rows for tier and local models lose their defaults, and the design also takes on Ollama availability per operation, safe settings writes and a restart-pending state.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
The main thread reads the definitions, the store and the settings once at boot into an immutable snapshot and passes it to every worker, including replacements; settings rows without a default are added so reconcile never writes a model choice; every operation that may run Ollama checks its installed list first; config.write and the updater are hardened, and clients track a restart-pending flag.

This was reviewed through review cycles 3 and 4; each round found another place the snapshot, the default-less rows or the extra scope did not reach (eagerly loaded embedder settings, the updater's catalog loader, older plugins reading row defaults, concurrent writers).
pros: A replacement worker can never pick up a settings change before a restart.
A fresh install's unset tiers follow later default changes.
cons: Requires changes to the settings catalog loader, reconcile, the updater, worker start-up and every eager settings reader, and breaks older plugins that read row defaults.
Pulls existing settings-write and Ollama-availability behaviour into this Epic, beyond the DEF.
Three review cycles kept finding new gaps in it.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Meets the constraints on paper, but only once every worker input, eager reader, settings-catalog consumer and older client is adapted, which three review cycles could not establish; it also takes on settings-write and Ollama-availability work the DEF does not ask for.

erDefinition.narrative: The shipped file holds exactly one entry for each of the three families; each family owns its models and, for the CLI families, its tier defaults, while the Ollama family names its tool-loop default. Defaults refer to a model of the same family by id or alias. A user's approved or rejected profile refers to one CLI family and lives outside the shipped file.

defaultFamily.description: The CLI family a fresh install and an Ollama tier's fallback use.

families.description: Exactly one entry per built-in family (one file to three families).

FamilyDefinition.description: A built-in family; owns its models and tier defaults.

cliKind.description: claude or codex; CLI families only.

summariserModel.description: Id or alias of one of this family's models (CLI families); many-to-one reference.

toolLoopModel.description: Ollama only: id of one of its listed models; many-to-one reference.

models.description: The family's selectable models (one family to many models).

tierDefaults.description: One default per tier; CLI families only.

ModelDefinition.description: One selectable model of exactly one family.

id.description: Canonical id, unique within its family.

aliases.description: Other names the CLI accepts, unique within the family.

efforts.description: Accepted effort levels; empty means none is passed.

inputLimit.description: Input limit and unit; required for Ollama models (the context window).

TierDefault.description: The default for one tier, owned by one CLI family.

model.description: Id or alias of a model of the owning family; many-to-one reference.

effort.description: Default effort; one the model accepts.

ApprovedProfile.description: A user's decision on one unknown Claude or Codex model, stored per user outside the shipped file (shape in sc2, written by sc4); many profiles may refer to one family.

family.description: The CLI family checked against; many-to-one reference.

modelId.description: A model id not listed for that family.

efforts.description: Approved only: levels that passed and the user approved.

inputLimit.description: From the CLI's output, when it states one.

cliVersion.description: CLI version the check ran against.
